content.text:
I couldn't open any files, so this diagnosis is inferred from the file list and the usual layout of this NestJS boilerplate. The line ranges are estimates.

The most likely cause is that a partial update, such as one that only changes `firstName`, is merged and mapped back to a persistence entity. The photo is then lost or set to `null`, because "photo not provided" isn't told apart from "photo cleared".

candidates.explanation: On a partial update (e.g. only firstName), the merged domain object reaches toPersistence. If photo is undefined, the mapper turns it into null, or drops the file relation. TypeORM save() then writes photoId = NULL, so the avatar disappears. The mapper should only map photo to null when domain.photo === null, and should leave it undefined when it wasn't provided.

The update merges the existing entity's domain object with the payload and saves the whole entity. If the payload carries an undefined or null photo, or the merge overwrites the existing photo, the stored photo is cleared on every partial update. Only fields actually present in the payload should be merged.

The profile update (PATCH /auth/me) builds the payload from the DTO and handles photo separately. If photo isn't supplied, the code can still set or pass userDto.photo as undefined or null into usersService.update, which overwrites the existing photo. The photo should only be touched when the DTO includes it.

fix.description: In toPersistence, set photo only when it was provided: if domain.photo is truthy, build the FileEntity; else if domain.photo === null, set null; otherwise leave it undefined so TypeORM doesn't touch the column. In the repository update, merge only the defined payload fields so omitted fields like photo keep their existing values. Do the same in AuthService.update and UsersService.update, where the photo should be resolved and assigned only if userDto.photo !== undefined.
